invariants: Backend is the canonical identity, session, authorization and product-data authority.
Data Centre owns infrastructure and storage mechanics, never product authorization.
CDN delivers bytes; it does not decide product visibility or ownership.
Algorithm ranks only Backend-authorized candidate IDs and cannot hydrate canonical records.
Federation owns protocol state and signed delivery, not local identity or canonical product records.
Flutter never receives private service tokens, provider credentials, database credentials or private service URLs.
The API control plane is build-time governance only and is never a runtime gateway.
No external identity provider is part of the supported runtime; native Testagram Backend authentication is the only user and staff authentication path.
All six runtime source pins identify exact current mainline commits; production and product acceptance remain independent gates.
No message or call is advertised as end-to-end encrypted until the reviewed client protocol, device trust, key lifecycle and media lifecycle pass end-to-end acceptance.
The video service has no host-published port; only Backend API, PostgreSQL and the Data Centre video service join the internal video-private network, while Caddy remains off it.
Video deletion commits product metadata removal and a durable media-cleanup outbox intent atomically; physical media cleanup is asynchronous, lease-recoverable and retryable.

Ordinary public signup, email verification, password login, session refresh, recovery and logout never require government ID, ID number, selfie, identity evidence, identity review, identity approval, or identity-evidence storage; optional identity assurance may gate only specifically designated sensitive capabilities.
